To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concept of im-brication can be used to inform design of services that are imbricated and that this can improve upon the sociomateriality of family trip planning.

1) the concept of imbri- cation can be used to inform design of services that are digitally material, 2) imbrications of digital and non-digital services can be designed to improve the materiality of family practices such as trip planning, and 3) the concept of digital `tells', and online remains are useful in designing digitally material family practices.
the imbrication of online remains with digital `telling' and `tells' may enhance the digital materiality in certain family practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how digital materiality of services can be designed to support family practices in a sociomaterial context.
exploring the potential of sociomaterial configurations of services in the context of family practices.
the design of interactive services that are imbricated with other digital and non-digital services and how these imbrications can be used to enhance digital materiality of family practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
imbrications of service and digital tells and remains can be used to improve the digital materiality in family practices such as trip planning.
the paper provides a theoretical scaffold for designing digital materials that can be imbricated into existing sociomaterial configurations of family practices.

this paper contributes to the field of HCI by providing a conceptual scaffold for the design of interactive services which exhibit digital materiality and which are informed by the concept of sociomateriality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the concept of sociomateriality provides a powerful lens for understanding how digital materiality can be used in the design and implementation of interactive systems that improve family practices.
digital materiality is a design concern that is informed by sociomateriality.
the imbrication of service and the use of digital materiality can be an effective way of designing for sociomaterial configurations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital materiality can be designed to support the co-evolution of human and nonhuman actors in a sociomaterial context.
the concept of imbri- cation is a promising theoretical lens to explore the design of digital materiality.
the concept of imbri-cation can be used to inform design of interactive systems which exhibit digital materiality and can be used to support the enactment of distributed organizing.
